- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce peak overshoots by 5–10% to avoid overreacting to sentiment-driven momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.3) and forecast is falling, avoid premature bottoming — maintain 1–2 price points above true low to account for volatility lag.
- After a spike in sentiment (e.g., 1.00), model should not overcorrect — cap forecast decline to 3–5% below peak to prevent mean reversion overcorrection.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows early mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days after peak), reduce forecast slope downward by 10–15% to reflect diminishing momentum.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00/0.33 patterns, model should not assume trend continuation — apply conservative smoothing to avoid false breakout signals.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.25) and forecast is trending, reduce forecast amplitude by 5–8% to account for low conviction and reduced volatility.
